question_text: A 53-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her husband because of difficulty walking, slurred speech, and progressive drowsiness. The husband reports that his wife has appeared depressed over the past few days. She has a history of insomnia and social anxiety disorder. She appears lethargic. Her temperature is 36.2°C (97.1°F), pulse is 88/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Neurologic examination shows normal pupils. There is diffuse hypotonia and decreased deep tendon reflexes. Administration of a drug that acts as a competitive antagonist at which of the following receptors is most likely to reverse this patient's symptoms?
